checks.what: An archaeon on its own: its size and how fast it divides
checks.real: The Asgard archaeon grown by Imachi and colleagues: 0.3 to 0.75 µm across, divides every 14 to 25 days

checks.what: Without the merger, archaea stay small and simple
checks.model: after 300,000 generations: 3,624 genes, 0.056 µm³, no eukaryotic feature complete
checks.real: No archaeon or bacterium has a nucleus, an inner membrane system and phagocytosis; Asgard archaea carry only some of the genes for them

checks.what: One merger founds every cell at the end
checks.model: 2 archaea took a partner inside; at the end every cell descends from one of them
checks.real: All mitochondria descend from one alphaproteobacterium

checks.what: Genes left in the guest genome at the end
checks.model: 50 genes, 29 of them for proteins: 0.97 % of the 3,000 protein genes it started with
checks.real: 37 in humans (13 for proteins) up to 100 in the protist Andalucia (66 for proteins); free-living relatives have thousands
checks.source: Anderson et al. 1981; Burger et al. 2013

checks.what: The genes that stay are the oily core of the respiratory chain
checks.model: cox1 and cob kept; kept proteins have 4.5 helices in the membrane on average, moved ones 0.58
checks.real: cox1 and cob stay in almost every mitochondrial genome; the proteins mitochondria still make are the most membrane-bound subunits

checks.what: Without protein import, the guest genome stops shrinking much sooner
checks.model: 733 genes left, 15 times as many as with import
checks.real: Insect endosymbionts, whose hosts send in few proteins, keep about 120 to 650 genes; mitochondria keep a handful to 100

checks.what: Genes in the host genome at the end
checks.real: Free-living protists have 6,000 to 40,000 genes (yeast about 6,000, Naegleria about 16,000); Asgard archaea about 4,000 to 5,000
checks.source: Goffeau et al. 1996; Fritz-Laylin et al. 2010; Spang et al. 2015

checks.what: How big the cells grow, compared with a bacterium
checks.model: 10,000 µm³, 27 µm across: 10,000 times the bacterium
checks.real: An average protist has about 15,000 times the mass of an average bacterium (accept 1,500 to 150,000)

checks.what: Power per gene, compared with a bacterium
checks.real: Four to five orders of magnitude more: 10,000 to 100,000 times as much (accept 3,000 to 300,000)
checks.note: Nothing aims at this number, but it rests on the cell size and genome size, which were tuned.

checks.what: Share of the cell taken up by mitochondria
checks.real: From about 8 % of a white blood cell to 22 % of a liver cell and nearly half of a heart muscle cell (accept 5 to 50 %)
